title: The Power of Repeated Words
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This entry examines how repeated words or phrases — mantras, affirmations, single-word cues — can shape performance under pressure by interrupting negative or anxious thought patterns. It traces the idea across Eastern spiritual traditions and Western performance psychology, framing repetition as a mechanism that gives the mind something structured to hold onto instead of wandering into self-doubt. The piece distinguishes purely instructional self-talk ("turn your hips") from affirming repeated language, arguing the latter has a distinct calming and confidence-building effect. It closes by encouraging readers to identify a personal word or phrase in advance, before it's needed under pressure.
points: Repeated affirming words or phrases are presented as a practical tool for interrupting negative thought spirals during high-pressure performance.
The piece draws a line between mechanical self-instruction (directing physical action) and affirming repetition, arguing only the latter delivers the calming, confidence-building effect.
The mind is described as working by aligning words and thoughts with action, making deliberate word choice a lever leaders and performers can use on purpose.
Preparation matters: the recommended practice is to select a personal word or phrase in advance, not to improvise one in the moment of pressure.
quotes: The power of repeated words, via our inner voice, has been known for centuries to have a profound impact on the mind.
The mystical hymn of the mantra is often melodic and used as a spiritual tool in nearly every religious tradition.
Repeated affirmations, such as “I am strong and resilient” or “I trust the process,” direct the mind to act accordingly.
In truth, any word or expression that is positive, not mechanical (directing action, such as “Turn your hips”), and repeated in a consistent stream with the inner voice can have a profound impact.
Repeated words and expressions provide the comfort and confidence necessary for sustained performance.
We act in accordance with what we repeatedly say to ourselves. Choose what you say to yourself carefully.
